ai.title: Split run-agent-step into run-tool and get-file-reading-updates
ai.summary: Refactored `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts` by extracting tool execution logic into `backend/src/run-tool.ts` and file reading update logic into `backend/src/get-file-reading-updates.ts`. This decomposition isolates responsibilities for agent step processing, tool calls, and file context updates. The change is internal, affecting backend structure without altering user-facing behavior or APIs.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer bundles three jobs together when it takes a step: deciding which files to look at, running a tool, and updating what you can see. Instead, each job now lives in its own module, so if one part breaks, the others keep working. You would not notice anything different right away, but the system is now easier to maintain and less likely to choke when a file lookup or tool call takes time. The split is live today for anyone running a session behind the scenes.

ai.title: Remove Anthropic fallback, route Claude via OpenRouter
ai.summary: Deleted `anthropic-with-fallbacks.ts` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` dependency, routing all Claude models through OpenRouter via `openrouterModels` constants. Updated `claude.ts` to define local `TextBlock` type, decoupling system prompts from Anthropic SDK types. Affected `backend/src/llm-apis/` (claude, gemini-with-fallbacks, openrouter), `backend/src/admin/` (grade-runs, relabelRuns), and `backend/src/find-files/` (request-files-prompt). Model references shifted from `claudeModels.sonnet` to `models.openrouter_claude_sonnet_4` in eval and relabeling scripts.

eli5.text: If you use Claude models through this service, you'll now get them via OpenRouter instead of Anthropic's own API. The system dropped its old Anthropic connection and rerouted all Claude traffic through OpenRouter, which means the behind-the-scenes plumbing changed but the end result for you stays the same: you still get Claude responses. The change also tidied up how internal references to Claude models are written, and it's already in effect today.

If you use a service that tracks and bills AI chat messages, you'll see slightly higher cost estimates for each conversation. The change is already live and applies to all tracked messages, not just specific users or plans.

ai.title: Add provider order for sonnet 4
ai.summary: Extracted OpenRouter model initialization into `openRouterLanguageModel` helper. Added provider order ['Google', 'Anthropic', 'Amazon Bedrock'] for `openrouter_claude_sonnet_4`. This ensures consistent routing priority for Sonnet 4 requests. Internal refactor, no user-facing API changes.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant questions using the latest Claude model, the system now tries answering through Google first, then Amazon Bedrock if Google is unavailable, and only then falls back to the original Anthropic source. This reshuffles the order of providers behind the scenes so responses come from whichever service is fastest or available, without you noticing any difference except potentially quicker answers. The change also cleans up how those cloud services connect, keeping the system organized for future features, and it went live today.

ai.title: Remove duplicate code from merge
ai.summary: Removed duplicate definitions of `getInitialFiles`, `getFileReadingUpdates`, `getPrintedPaths`, and `uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining` from `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`. The file now imports `getFileReadingUpdates` from `./get-file-reading-updates`. Cleaned up unused imports including `requestFiles`, `parseFileBlocks`, `toContentString`, `countTokens`, `difference`, `uniq`, `CoreMessage`, `TextBlock`, `HIDDEN_FILE_READ_STATUS`, `requestRelevantFilesForTraining`, `GetExpandedFileContextForTrainingBlobTrace`, `parseToolResults`, `parseReadFilesResult`, and `insertTrace`. Scope limited to backend agent step execution logic.

eli5.text: The system that runs the AI assistant cleaned up its own internal instructions by removing a block of duplicate steps that had been pasted in twice. If you watched the assistant work, it would behave exactly the same; the cleanup only makes the behind-the-scenes logic shorter and easier for the engineers to maintain.

ai.title: Disable Amazon Bedrock for OpenRouter Claude Sonnet 4
ai.summary: Amazon Bedrock removed from provider routing order for `openrouter_claude_sonnet_4` in `backend/src/llm-apis/openrouter.ts`. Routing order now strictly prioritizes `Google` then `Anthropic` to avoid Bedrock-specific failures or latency. Change scoped to OpenRouter language model factory.

eli5.text: When you use the Claude Sonnet 4 model through OpenRouter, the system will no longer try Amazon Bedrock as a backup provider; it now only uses Google and Anthropic. This affects you if you rely on OpenRouter-powered Claude Sonnet 4 conversations, since any fallback that previously went to Amazon Bedrock is now skipped, potentially reducing certain timeout or latency issues specific to Bedrock. If you watched the routing behavior, you'd see fewer attempts to hand off to Bedrock, and more consistent use of the Google or Anthropic endpoints instead.

ai.title: Add opus provider order preference
ai.summary: Provider routing order preference added for `openrouter_claude_opus_4` in `backend/src/llm-apis/openrouter.ts`. `providerOrder` constant maps model IDs to provider arrays, replacing hardcoded check for `openrouter_claude_sonnet_4`. `extraBody.provider.order` now dynamically resolves via `providerOrder` lookup.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use a newer, more powerful version of Claude called Opus, the system now knows which service to try first for that model, just like it already did for the Sonnet version. You won't see anything different on your screen, but behind the scenes, the assistant now routes Opus requests through Google, then Anthropic, then Amazon Bedrock in that preferred order. If you were using Opus before this change, it may now behave more consistently with how Sonnet requests are handled.

eli5.text: Amazon Bedrock has been removed from the list of providers used to fulfill Opus 4 requests, leaving Google and Anthropic as the only routing options. ai.title: openrouter.ts: allowfallbacks false
ai.summary: Added `allow_fallbacks: false` to provider config in `openRouterLanguageModel`. Prevents OpenRouter fallbacks for ordered providers. Internal backend change.

eli5.text: The system that routes requests between different AI providers was told to stop trying backup options when a specific provider is listed. Previously, if an ordered provider failed, the system would automatically try other available providers as a fallback. Now, when a provider is explicitly ordered for a model, the system will only use that chosen provider and not fall back to others. This affects how reliably specific AI models are accessed through ordered provider configurations.

eli5.text: When Anthropic sends back a response through OpenRouter, the system now accepts a blank or empty cost value for that response instead of rejecting it outright. Previously, the system would balk at a missing or null cost from Anthropic, treating it as an error; now it simply moves on. You wouldn't see anything different unless you looked closely at the logs for Anthropic responses routed through OpenRouter, where the system no longer complains about that particular missing value.

ai.title: Upstream inference cost accepts null for Anthropic responses
ai.summary: The OpenRouter chat completion response schema now allows `upstream_inference_cost` inside `cost_details` to be null or missing via `z.number().nullish()` in `packages/internal/src/openrouter-ai-sdk/openrouter-chat-language-model.ts`. This handles Anthropic responses that return a nullish inference cost, avoiding strict-number validation rejection. The outer `cost_details` was already `.nullish()` and sibling `cost` remains `.optional()`, so only the inner field widens.

ai.title: Pin OpenRouter model IDs to dated versions
ai.summary: Updated `openrouterModels` in `common/src/constants.ts` to use explicit dated model IDs (e.g., `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522`) instead of generic aliases. This ensures deterministic model resolution and prevents unexpected behavior changes from upstream alias updates. Scope limited to shared core constants.

eli5.text: The assistant now uses specific dated versions of AI models instead of generic names, so the responses you get stay consistent over time rather than changing unexpectedly when the model provider updates what a generic name points to. For example, instead of referring to a model by a name that could silently switch to a newer version, the system now pins it down to a specific snapshot from a particular date, ensuring the behavior you experience today is the same behavior you'd get tomorrow. This affects anyone interacting with the assistant through OpenRouter, and while you won\'t see an obvious visual difference, you\'ll notice more reliable and predictable responses over time.
